faq_schema.q: Can spot the difference puzzles really help siblings get along?
faq_schema.a: Yes! When structured cooperatively, they encourage communication, patience, and shared success, reducing rivalry.

faq_schema.q: At what age can a child start spot the difference puzzles?
faq_schema.a: Most children begin around age 4 with simple, large-image puzzles; complexity increases with age.

faq_schema.q: How many differences should a puzzle have for mixed-age play?
faq_schema.a: Aim for 5–7 differences for ages 4–6, and 10–12 for ages 7–12; you can adjust by giving older kids fewer hints.

faq_schema.q: Are spot the difference puzzles good for the classroom?
faq_schema.a: Absolutely—they build observation, patience, and collaborative skills. Volume 2's school theme ties directly to classroom learning.

faq_schema.q: What if my children have very different skill levels?
faq_schema.a: Use timers or role-based play: older child explains strategies, younger child points; praise effort over speed.
